NAME: Improving Knowledge Liability Coverage
EXPRESSION: SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3), RATIO(lt, at)), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose organic R&D coverage of liabilities is improving while goodwill intensity is not rising are more likely building productive internally generated knowledge.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This shifts the strong but FMB-weak knowledge-coverage idea from a static level to an improvement measure, which may better align cross-sectional slopes with future returns. The goodwill-change penalty distinguishes improving organic knowledge coverage from acquisition-accounting expansion.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Patient Acquisition Margin Realization
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltt, ADD(dltt, dlc))), MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 5), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Goodwill-heavy acquisition exposure is more likely productive when paired with patient debt maturity and improving gross-margin economics.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Prior levered-goodwill signals showed that goodwill highs are not uniformly negative, so this version requires evidence of acquisition realization rather than overhang. Long-maturity financing gives acquired intangible assets time to integrate, while margin improvement indicates operating payoff.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Current-Debt Ad Gross-Profit Strain
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(dlc, sale), 1)), RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(xad, SUB(revt, cogs)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Advertising becomes less productive when its burden on gross profit rises at the same time current debt per sales is increasing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This focuses on a rollover-financing strain mechanism rather than broad liability growth or advertising volatility. The signal asks whether customer-acquisition spending is consuming more gross-profit capacity while short-term financing pressure is rising.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Flexible Finance R&D Sales Option
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(lt, at), 5)), MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5)), RANK(GROWTH(revt, 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Financing variability can be valuable when it supports R&D near a firm’s own high-water mark and that R&D is converting into revenue growth.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This diagnoses the mixed evidence on financing volatility by treating it as flexibility only when paired with observable commercialization. A high signal identifies firms using variable financing capacity around an active R&D option set that is producing sales traction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Debt-Retirement R&D Margin Confirmation
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUB(RANK(RATIO(dltr, at)), RANK(RATIO(dltis, at))), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Debt retirement is more likely to predict productive intangible investment when rising R&D intensity is accompanied by improving gross margins.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The prior debt-retired R&D signal had strong cross-sectional evidence but weak portfolio evidence, suggesting that R&D continuity alone may not identify realizable value. Adding margin confirmation seeks firms where debt discipline and organic innovation are supported by improving product economics.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Maturity-Matched Identifiable Intangibles
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUB(RANK(RATIO(dltt, at)), RANK(RATIO(dlc, at))), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(intan, 0), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Growth in identifiable intangible assets is more valuable when financed with long-maturity rather than short-maturity debt.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Identifiable intangibles are more specific than residual goodwill and may provide clearer economic backing for financing. The maturity-matching leg tests whether patient financing supports intangible asset formation rather than forcing near-term refinancing pressure.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Patient Acquisition Margin Realization---

RATIONALE: It swaps the goodwill leg of the near-null "Flexible-Financed R&D Exercise" for revenue growth already used in "Nondilutive R&D Revenue Conversion" and "Self-Financing R&D Commercialization," and the reinterpretation of liability-ratio volatility as "flexibility" is asserted rather than argued, leaving a three-way all-positive rank product with no clear economic direction.

---CRITIQUE Debt-Retirement R&D Margin Confirmation---

NAME: Debt-Overhang R&D Crowding Out
EXPRESSION: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(lt, at), 5), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms near their own liability-overhang highs with declining R&D intensity are likely cutting intangible investment because financing pressure is crowding out innovation.

NAME: Post-Acquisition Debt Cleanup
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(SUB(RATIO(dltr, at), RATIO(dltis, at))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that reduce debt while goodwill intensity falls are more likely digesting prior acquisitions successfully rather than carrying externally financed acquisition overhang.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This avoids the unidentified all-positive goodwill-realization product by focusing on post-acquisition balance-sheet repair. A high score requires both net debt retirement and declining goodwill exposure, consistent with integration discipline or reduced overpayment risk.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Rollover Brand-Capital Cut
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(dlc, at), 1)), MUL(RANK(LAG(MA(RATIO(xad, sale), 3), 1)), RANK(NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(xad, sale), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Rising current-debt pressure is especially negative when established advertisers cut advertising intensity, suggesting rollover financing is forcing customer-capital underinvestment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This is not another advertising burden per gross-profit signal; it tests a brand-capital crowd-out mechanism. The lagged advertising level ensures that the cut is economically meaningful for firms with prior brand investment rather than a generic low-advertising sort.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Volatile-Finance R&D Margin Gap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(lt, at), 5)), SUB(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), sale), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Financing volatility is negative when R&D intensity is near a firm-specific high but gross margins are not improving, indicating uncertain funding of innovation without economic realization.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This does not assume liability volatility is good or bad unconditionally; it is bad when paired with high R&D commitment that lacks margin conversion. The signed R&D-minus-margin gap avoids the prior unidentified all-positive rank product and gives the interaction a clearer economic direction.
